To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Gas6‐A xl signaling in presence of sunitinib is intensified and diversified and specifically triggers downstream Akt and Pras40 activation in an amplified manner.
Gas6‐mediates Axl signaling is enhanced and diversified by Sunitinib in renal cancer cells and that this results in tumor‐progression.
Gas6‐mediatated Axl signaling is enhanced and diversified and sustained in the presence of sunitinib in renal tumor cells and endothelial cells.

the investigation of the role of Gas6‐A xl signaling in CCRC C and endothelial cells in presence of Sunt inib.
the identification and validation of novel therapeutic targets and biomarkers for the treatment of CCRCC and other cancers.
the role of Gas6‐Axi signaling in CCRC cells in the context of Sunitinibs treatment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

Gas6‐Axi signaling, which is intensified and diversified in the Sunitinib treated cells, might contribute to acquired chemoresistant and aggressive behavior of CCRCC, and that targeting of Axi signaling might be beneficial in the treatment of Sunitinb intended CCRCC patients.
Gas6‐mediates Axl signaling in Sunitinibtreated CCRCC and HUVECs is intensified and sustained and specifically triggers downstream PRAS40 and AKT activation.
